decisive_items: monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
response.rationale: The histopathologic findings of atypical lymphocytes, a CD4-predominant infiltrate with loss of CD8, and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement are diagnostic of mycosis fungoides, a specific cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Follicular mucin deposition is a secondary feature often seen in folliculotropic mycosis fungoides. R3 (Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) is a broader category, while R2 (Follicular mucinosis) lacks the atypical and clonal features.

rejected.why: Follicular mucinosis alone is a benign condition; the presence of atypical lymphocytes and clonal T-cell rearrangement indicates a neoplastic process, specifically mycosis fungoides.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is a valid but less specific diagnosis; mycosis fungoides is the precise entity supported by the clinical and histopathologic features.
